name: Alioth
description: A giant of type A1 III-IV 24.3 parsecs away, 4.3 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2023), AJ 166, 268, HD 112185: radius 4.29 +0.19/-0.21 solar radii (Table 7), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.644 +/- 0.02 mas (NPOI, Table 5) and the Gaia DR2 (Gaia Collaboration 2018) parallax

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2023), AJ 166, 268, HD 112185: effective temperature 8908 +/- 54 K (Table 7), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

gravity.source: Baines et al. (2023), AJ 166, 268, HD 112185: log g 3.59, from McDonald et al. (2017), as the paper lists it beside the diameter (Table 5)

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331, XHIP, HIP 62956: RV -12.7 +/- 0.2 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: Baines et al. (2023), AJ 166, 268, HD 112185: the Gaia DR2 (Gaia Collaboration 2018) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 2), 41.22 +/- 1.84 mas, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A giant of type A1 III-IV, 24 parsecs away: 4.3 times the Sun's width and 104 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.644 milliarcseconds, which gives 4.29 solar radii and 8,908 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 2, 5 and 7, HD 112185: parallax, MK type, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff, luminosity
